text: Large language models, or LLMs, are computer programs that can understand and produce human language. They work by predicting the next word in a sentence, based on patterns they learned from huge amounts of training data, such as books, websites and articles. Users can improve results through prompt engineering, which means writing clear and specific instructions. LLMs are very good at tasks like summarising texts, translating languages and answering questions. However, they also have limits. They sometimes give wrong information, they cannot truly understand meaning, and their knowledge stops at the date of their training data.
